title: The second eigenvalue changes the decay
hook: Two stated cases: explore the spectral-gap facet of a two-state mixing model.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How the spectral-gap facet of a two-state mixing model affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines TV, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare the spectral-gap facet of a two-state mixing model in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: A toy two-state chain transitions 0→1 with A 0.01, 1→0 with B 0.01; initial P(1) 1. After 10 steps, what is total-variation distance from stationarity?

claims.text: The nontrivial eigenvalue controls the transient distance in this two-state model. A stationary distribution can exist even when periodicity prevents convergence. This comparison isolates the spectral-gap facet of a two-state mixing model.
